questions.prompt: In What Is Express.js?, which statement best describes Express applications and HTTP servers?
options: Move all backend decisions into the browser and trust the submitted values.
Return the same success response for every request regardless of outcome.
Keep the interface predictable for its client: use clear resource boundaries, explicit request/response formats, correct status codes, validation and tests for failure cases.
Keep the layers distinct: Node.js runs JavaScript and provides runtime APIs; Express builds request routing and middleware behavior on top of that runtime.
questions.answer_key: Keep the interface predictable for its client: use clear resource boundaries, explicit request/response formats, correct status codes, validation and tests for failure cases.
questions.explanation: Keep the interface predictable for its client: use clear resource boundaries, explicit request/response formats, correct status codes, validation and tests for failure cases.

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying What Is Express.js??
options: Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.

Express is a web framework layered on the Node.js runtime. Start by tracing one HTTP request through a route handler, middleware, and response, and keep framework features separate from packages in the broader ecosystem.
Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
questions.answer_key: Express is a web framework layered on the Node.js runtime. Start by tracing one HTTP request through a route handler, middleware, and response, and keep framework features separate from packages in the broader ecosystem.
questions.explanation: Express is a web framework layered on the Node.js runtime. Start by tracing one HTTP request through a route handler, middleware, and response, and keep framework features separate from packages in the broader ecosystem.

questions.prompt: A change related to What Is Express.js? appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?
options: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
Test only one successful request manually and record no expected output.
Use production data to avoid building a small reproducible fixture.
Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.
questions.answer_key: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
questions.explanation: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
